params.name: Size-class Sealed Body lengths (P-FMT-1)
params.production: Same table if the measured Admission Slot A is at most 1,024 B; if A exceeds 1,024 B, classes 1-3 only (1,024, 4,096, 16,384 B)
params.reason: DEC-013. One table serves the overlay and the ledger carrier (1, 4, 16 and 64 Misc parts, MPE-FMT-041). The 256 B class keeps full-feed cost low (o3 R2, g3 R2). DEC-FMT-1's own trigger removes class 0 when admission overhead dominates it. PRF fixtures stated as '4 KiB complete Envelopes' map to class 2 (wire 4,616 B).

params.name: Admission Slot width A (P-FMT-2)
params.prototype: 512 B: epoch 8 B, membership root 32 B, nullifier 32 B, share y 32 B, proof 256 B (360 B), then zero fill
params.production: Measured length of the selected proof fields rounded up to a multiple of 64 B, at most 4,096 B (P-ECO-11), fixed per version
params.reason: The Waku RateLimitProof carries a 256 B uncompressed (128 B compressed) proof and 32 B root, shares and nullifier (2021-vac-waku2-rln-relay-spec, RateLimitProof table); share x is recomputed from the Envelope Identifier (MPE-ECO-018), so it is not sent. s2's object-bound stamp is 354 B (2024-rfc9578-privacypass-issuance section 6.3, per P-FMT-2). 512 B fits both and leaves 152 B for a different proof encoding without changing the class table. Unused bytes must be zero (new MPE-FMT-050).

params.name: Visible Header and wire length
params.prototype: 8 B fixed fields + 512 B Admission Slot = 520 B; wire 776, 1,544, 4,616, 16,904 B
params.production: 8 B + A; wire = 8 + A + class body
params.reason: DEC-FMT-2 option (a). g1's 192 B, g2's 211 B and o4's 304 B headers are rejected with their visible tags, clues, member keys and msg_id. CRY's salt, nonce and Tag move to the clear prefix of the Sealed Body (new MPE-FMT-051), so the CRY-004 'pre-seal header' is the Network Identifier, header bytes 0-7 and that prefix.

params.name: Payload capacity per class (default cryptographic profile)
params.production: Class body minus 170 B for the default profile; recomputed from MPE-CRY-036 for any other profile
params.reason: Sealed Body = 44 B clear prefix (salt 16, nonce 12, Tag 16) + ciphertext. Plaintext = 40 B Sealed Prefix + 70 B authentication block (new MPE-CRY-041: key index 2, creation time 4, Ed25519 signature 64) + payload + zero padding; the AEAD adds 16 B. 256 - 44 - 16 - 40 - 70 = 86 B. DEC-FMT-7's 156 B figure assumed an X25519 key that the symmetric default does not carry and omitted the signature.

params.name: GossipSub maximum transmit size (P-FMT-6, P-NET-8)
params.reason: Largest wire is 16,904 B in the prototype and 20,488 B at A = 4,096 B. rust-libp2p default (rust-libp2p/protocols/gossipsub/src/protocol.rs:100). NET's allowed range up to 262,144 B serves only g2's 256 KiB class, which no area adopts.

params.name: Maximum Envelope lifetime L_max (P-FMT-3)
params.reason: DEC-004. g3, s1, s3 and s4 converge on 48 h; the ceiling is global_ttl (midnight-node/res/mainnet/ledger-parameters-config.json:176). PUB's L_max is this parameter.

params.name: Ordinary retention (P-STO-1) and retention deadline
params.prototype: Retention deadline = visible expiry, at most P-FMT-3 + P-FMT-4 after arrival
params.production: Same; optional paid archive up to 604,800 s (P-STO-7)
params.reason: A Store Node sees no creation time: it is signed inside the seal (MPE-CRY-021) and the Visible Header carries only expiry (MPE-FMT-003). STO-003 as written cannot be evaluated by a Store Node.

params.name: Expiry clock tolerance (P-FMT-4; replaces P-PUB-8 in delivery rules)
params.reason: The same expired-on-arrival check carried 60 s (MPE-FMT-030) and 120 s (MPE-PUB-029). 60 s exceeds normal NTP error; chain-view staleness has its own threshold (P-NET-13). P-PUB-8 is retired.

params.name: Chain-view staleness threshold (P-NET-13; absorbs P-FMT-5 and P-OPS-10)
params.reason: Three definitions existed: clock against latest finalized block above 120 s (FMT-031, NET-019), Registry lag above 60 s (OPS-022) and 'newest root older than P-ECO-5 = 3,600 s' (ECO-024). After DEC-009 a stale view only turns chain-dependent Reject into Ignore and keeps cached-valid forwarding, so an early trigger costs little. 60 s is 10 slots of 6 s (midnight-node/runtime/src/lib.rs:292) and more than three times the 18 s finality (notes/midnight-network-stack.md section 1.7).

params.name: Membership-root acceptance window (P-ECO-5)
params.prototype: 3,600 s counted from the root's supersession; the current root is always eligible
params.reason: ECO-015 counts from publication, so a Registry with no registration for one hour would make every Envelope Ignore. Supersession time is recorded alongside publication time (MPE-ECO-027, new MPE-NET-055).

params.name: Stale-root bound (P-ECO-4 + P-ECO-5)
params.reason: Bounds forwarding under a cached root while the chain view is stale (DEC-009): a root becomes ineligible P-ECO-5 after the membership period it serves ends (new MPE-ECO-051). 86,400 s + 3,600 s = 90,000 s.

params.name: Admission epoch and tolerance (P-ECO-1, P-ECO-6)
params.reason: DEC-ECO-5 (o1, o2, o4). The publish retry budget P-PUB-5 x P-PUB-6 = 5 s x 3 = 15 s stays inside the 20 s tolerance, so identical retransmissions started in an epoch's last second remain admissible; new MPE-PUB-053 stops retries beyond that.

params.name: Nullifier retention and restart barrier (P-ECO-7)
params.reason: 2 x 60 s + 20 s. An allowance is permanently ineligible 80 s after its epoch ends, at most 140 s after acceptance. Refusing live admission for 140 s after each start (DEC-017) restores the replay invariant without a disk write on the forwarding path. SEC-017 and STO-014 state the same bound without a number.

params.name: Membership period (P-ECO-4)
params.reason: Daily renewal costs about 0.1 DUST/day against 2.4 for hourly renewal (g3). Ceiling: 10% of 1,000,000 blockUsage bytes per block (ledger-parameters-config.json:158) over 14,400 blocks/day is 1.44 GB/day; at the 16 KiB registration gate (P-ECO-13) that is 1,440,000,000 / 16,384 = 87,890 registrations per day before Anchors.

params.name: Lowest-tier publication quota (P-ECO-2, P-ECO-3)
params.prototype: Per-class limits (64, 16, 4, 1) Envelopes per epoch for classes 0-3, committed in the membership leaf; one nullifier per Envelope
params.production: Same vector; an exact 64-credit byte debit (credit = 256 B of body) only if a multi-nullifier circuit passes P-ECO-11 and P-ECO-12
params.reason: DEC-016. P-ECO-2 = 10 credits is below the class-3 weight of 64 (P-ECO-3), so ECO-017 as written forbids class 3 to the lowest tier, and it needs up to 64 nullifier and share pairs per Envelope, which one fixed Admission Slot cannot hold. The vector gives 16,384 B of body per class per epoch (273 B/s): 240 single-class memberships, or 60 using all four classes, saturate one 64 KiB/s Shard.

params.name: Per-Shard capacity (P-PRF-1, P-PRF-2, P-VER-2)
params.prototype: 10 Envelopes/s and 64 KiB/s per Shard, whichever binds first
params.reason: DEC-005. At 10/s the byte cap binds above a mean wire size of 6,553.6 B; with prototype wire sizes class 3 alone binds at 65,536 / 16,904 = 3.88 Envelopes/s.

params.name: Comparison and burst loads (P-PRF-28, P-PRF-29, P-VER-4, P-VER-5, P-VER-9, P-VER-10)
params.prototype: 50 Envelopes/s for 24 h as a comparison; 100 Envelopes/s per Shard for 60 s as a burst
params.reason: g1's normalized mix (847.7 B mean) at 50/s is 41.39 KiB/s, inside the byte cap and above the count cap; the run decides whether the count ceiling can rise (DEC-005).

params.name: Shard count (P-PUB-1, P-NET-9)
params.reason: DEC-011. Nine Round 2 votes favour one feed (DEC-PUB-1). P-PUB-1 allowed 1-16 and P-NET-9 1-8; no proponent of 16 Shards (o1, o2) remains after Round 2.

params.name: Mesh tuple D, D_lo, D_hi, D_out (P-NET-1..4, P-PRF-4, P-SEC-1)
params.reason: DEC-012. The prototype gates include a 20% cold-start Sybil attack (MPE-PRF-032, MPE-VER-018) and an outbound quota of 4 (MPE-SEC-003); (8, 6, 12, 4) is the profile evaluated under Sybil cold start (2020-vyzovitis-gossipsub). It satisfies D_out < D_lo and D_out <= D/2 (specs/pubsub/gossipsub/gossipsub-v1.1.md:192).

params.name: Heartbeat, gossip factor, prune backoff, flood publishing
params.reason: Consistent across NET, PRF and SEC. Flood publishing off departs from the specification default (specs/pubsub/gossipsub/gossipsub-v1.1.md:549; rust-libp2p/protocols/gossipsub/src/config.rs:548).

params.name: Edge Bus Node bandwidth (P-PRF-12)
params.prototype: At most 6 Mbit/s egress and 6 Mbit/s ingress at one Shard's byte cap
params.reason: g3's planning model is egress: 1.25 x D x 64 KiB/s (g3 R1 D5: '1.25 x 6 x 64 KiB/s = 480 KiB/s, about 3.9 Mbit/s'). With D = 8: 1.25 x 8 x 65,536 B/s x 8 bit = 5.24 Mbit/s, which breaks the 4 Mbit/s figure. Ingress carries the same duplicates. A per-direction budget settles DEC-PRF-4's direction question.

params.name: Full Bus Node bandwidth (P-PRF-13)
params.prototype: At most 24 Mbit/s per direction with 4 Shards at their byte caps
params.reason: 4 x 5.24 = 20.97 Mbit/s planning egress plus headroom; g3's 16 Mbit/s was its D = 6 egress model.

params.name: Bus Node CPU (P-PRF-14, P-PRF-15)
params.reason: 10 Envelopes/s x 4.5 ms Groth16 verification on a 4-vCPU VM (2024-revuelta-waku-latency Table 1) is 0.045 core per Shard; at the P-ECO-12 gate of 10 ms it is 0.10 core, inside 0.30.

params.name: Bus Node memory ceiling (new P-PRF-34)
params.reason: MPE-VER-015 cannot pass without a ceiling. Application seen-set at one Shard: 10/s x 172,860 s = 1.73 million identifiers x about 72 B = 124 MB; 4 Shards about 0.5 GB, inside P-STO-4 = 1 GiB; plus 1 GiB for process, GossipSub caches and queues (P-SEC-4 x 16,904 B = 2.2 MB). New MPE-PRF-041.

params.name: Bus Node application seen-set retention (MPE-PUB-027, P-STO-6)
params.reason: A Bus Node Ignores anything whose expiry is earlier than its clock minus P-FMT-4 (MPE-FMT-030), so longer retention protects nothing. P-STO-6 (+3,600 s) and P-PUB-8 (+120 s) disagreed; P-STO-6 is retired.

params.name: Client deduplication retention (P-CON-2)
params.reason: Clients receive back-fill pages up to P-STO-2 after expiry and apply no expiry gate before recognition; one hour covers client clock error.

params.name: Recognition key cap (P-CRY-4, P-PUB-4, P-CON-7)
params.reason: Same default in three files; PUB and CON ranges up to 4,096 exceed CRY's bound. Cost at the cap: 256 keys x 10 Envelopes/s = 2,560 HMAC-SHA-256 evaluations per second.

params.name: Tag and salt (P-CRY-2, P-CRY-3; withdraws P-CON-5, P-CON-6)
params.prototype: 16 B Tag and 16 B salt in the Sealed Body clear prefix
params.reason: DEC-003. Salted per-Envelope Tags make the expected-Tag lookahead window and the recognition-window gap unnecessary.

params.name: Sequence-gap wait (P-PUB-7; withdraws P-CON-1)
params.reason: A missing Envelope is repaired by reconciliation every 60 s (P-PUB-3) plus delivery within 10 s (P-VER-6): 70 s. CON's 60 s would emit gap items that the next reconciliation fills.

params.name: Reconciliation interval and independent sources (P-PUB-3, P-CON-4, P-CON-3, P-SEC-2)
params.prototype: 60 s; 2 sources from distinct mock Operators
params.reason: Inventory at 10/s: 600 identifiers x 32 B = 19,200 B per minute, 27.6 MB/day, 1.6% of a 1.77 GB/day feed (DEC-PUB-4). Priority conflict resolved by DEC-025.

params.name: Full-Shard streams per Bus Node (P-PUB-10, P-PRF-17)
params.reason: At the byte cap one stream is 0.524 Mbit/s; 8 streams need 4.19 Mbit/s on top of 5.24 Mbit/s mesh egress. MPE-PRF-036 still refuses streams beyond remaining bandwidth.

params.name: Per-peer pre-verification rate (P-ECO-10, P-NET-10)
params.reason: A per-peer total starves Full Bus Nodes: a mesh peer on 4 Shards at capacity forwards up to 40 Envelopes/s. 20/s per Shard is twice the Shard cap.

params.name: Verification queues (P-SEC-3, P-SEC-4)
params.reason: 128 x 16,904 B = 2.2 MB; at 4.5 ms per proof a full queue drains in 0.58 s, below the 3 s p99 target.

params.name: Publisher retry (P-PUB-5, P-PUB-6)
params.reason: 15 s total, inside the 20 s epoch tolerance (P-ECO-6) and above the 3 s propagation p99.

params.name: Latency gates (P-PRF-10, P-PRF-11, P-VER-6, P-VER-7, P-VER-21..23)
params.prototype: Post-admission delivery p99 at most 10 s and at least 99.9% of eligible pairs within 10 s; warm propagation p50 1.5 s and p99 3 s recorded, a miss triggers MPE-PRF-011
params.production: Warm propagation p50 at most 1.5 s and p99 at most 3 s; canary delivery at least 99.9% within 5 s for 30 consecutive days
params.reason: DEC-PRF-3 and DEC-VER-2. The prototype carries unmeasured admission costs, so g3's 3 s target is recorded rather than gated; production adopts it with o4's canary window. MPE-PRF-007 and MPE-PRF-023 receive the 10 s deadline they lacked.

params.name: Attack thresholds (P-PRF-22..24, P-VER-25, P-OPS-5)
params.prototype: 20% cold-start Sybil: at least 99% delivery and completed p99 at most 6 s; failure at 200 nodes triggers MPE-PRF-038
params.production: Open-admission red team at 1:1 Sybil identities: canary delivery at least 99.9% (P-OPS-5)
params.reason: MPE-VER-040 used 99% and MPE-OPS-008 used 99.9% for the same gate. Removing a safety restriction takes the stricter value, which equals the canary SLO.

params.name: Adversarial fractions (P-SEC-6, P-PRV-1, P-VER-11, P-VER-12, P-PRF-22)
params.production: Same sets for the red team
params.reason: Union of the five sets; DEC-NET-6 asks for a 10% spy run.

params.name: Soak duration (P-PRF-25, P-VER-3)
params.reason: A Store Node reaches steady-state storage only after one 48 h retention window; 72 h = 48 h fill + 24 h of pruning at steady state. P-PRF-25 said 48 h.

params.name: Topology sizes (P-VER-1, P-PRF-9, P-VER-8)
params.prototype: 32 local Bus Node processes for reference runs (at least 16 for MPE-VER-011); simulations at 50, 200 and 1,000
params.reason: P-PRF-9 reference conditions use 32 Bus Nodes per Shard; 32 satisfies VER's minimum of 16.

params.name: Store Node allocation (P-STO-3) and Bus Node caches (P-STO-4)
params.reason: Byte cap x 48 h = 65,536 x 172,800 = 11,324,620,800 B = 10.55 GiB raw; 21.1 GiB at the assumed 2x database multiplier.

params.name: Distinct Operators for 'stored' (P-STO-5)
params.reason: MPE-STO-012 is a POC MUST and cannot execute without Operator diversity in the mock roster.

params.name: Anchor window and granularity (P-NET-17)
params.prototype: 60 s; one Anchor per non-empty window covering every Shard
params.reason: DEC-024. NET-041 (one per Shard per window) and STO's record bound (one per window) differ by the Shard count. A combined payload (8 B window, 32 B root, 4 B count per Shard = 72 B at 8 Shards) fits the 256 B Misc payload (MPE-FMT-047). Cost: 1,440 Anchors/day; at the 8 KiB transaction assumed in DEC-PRF-6, 11.8 MB/day = 0.08% of 14.4 GB/day blockUsage.

params.name: Live Anchor history (P-STO-9, P-STO-10)
params.reason: Consumption rejects expired Events (MPE-CON-046), so no contract needs a root older than L_max; 1 h margin. 49 h x 60 windows per hour = 2,940. o4's 7 days and o2's 14 days assumed 7- to 14-day lifetimes.

params.name: Unanchored wait (P-CON-8)
params.reason: 60 s window + 6 s inclusion + about 18 s finality + indexing, with margin.

params.name: Tombstone deadline (P-SEC-5, P-STO-14, P-OPS-13)
params.reason: DEC-018. With 48 h retention a 48 h deadline never removes a body before ordinary expiry; 24 h is inside all three allowed ranges.

params.name: Version overlap (P-FMT-9, P-OPS-19)
params.reason: Identical definitions; MPE-OPS-035 becomes see canonical MPE-FMT-024.

params.name: Bootstrappers (P-OPS-3, P-NET-11, P-SEC-2)
params.production: 4, each run by a distinct Operator
params.reason: NET-025 already requires distinct Operators; this satisfies SEC's minimum of 2.

params.name: Launch relay roster (P-OPS-1, P-OPS-2)
params.prototype: Mock roster of at least 3 organizations
params.production: At least 8 organizations; at most 20% of listed relays each
params.reason: DEC-OPS-6; s1 and o4 R2 back 8 organizations.

params.name: Chain-share budget (P-ECO-8)
params.production: 10% of blockUsage, 24 h mean, enforced by client back-off
params.reason: Anchors at 60 s use 0.08%; the remainder bounds registrations (87,890 per day at 16 KiB).

params.name: Skipped-key retention (P-CRY-7)
params.production: 172,800 s; 604,800 s only where an archive profile is enabled
params.reason: Keys need to outlive only the ciphertext the client can still fetch; shorter retention narrows compromise exposure (2016-signal-double-ratchet-spec section 8.4).

params.name: Bond and deposit amounts (P-ECO-14..17)
params.production: None at launch; if enabled, amount set from the MPE-ECO-050 flood cost, withdrawal delay 7 days, reporter share at most 10%
params.reason: DEC-007: revocation is the launch deterrent; contract-held NIGHT on mainnet is unknown.

params.name: Admission gates (P-ECO-11, P-ECO-12, P-ECO-13)
params.prototype: Encoded Admission Slot at most 4,096 B (a proof of at most 3,992 B); verification at most 10 ms on one core of a 4-vCPU VM
params.production: Same, plus registration at most 16 KiB and 0.5 DUST
params.reason: Consistent across ECO, FMT and OPS.

params.name: Chaos, race and usability fixtures (P-VER-13/P-CON-10, P-VER-17/P-CON-12, P-VER-18..20/P-CON-13)
params.prototype: 1,000,000 Events; 100 reactors; 4 of 5 developers within 4 h
params.reason: Identical values; the CON copies become see canonical.

decisions.title: Who pays relays and other Operators
options: (b) Off-protocol contracts for relays, gateways and issuers
(c) Registry treasury paying only contract-checkable work (Anchors, passed retention challenges)
(d) Pool paid on multi-monitor probe scores

proposed_by.(a): g1, g2, g3, g4, o3; DEC-ECO-3(a), DEC-OPS-3(a)
proposed_by.(b): s1, s2, s3, s4; DEC-ECO-3(b), DEC-OPS-3(b)

decisions.prototype_default: (a): no payment code; MPE-ECO-037 and MPE-ECO-038 hold.
decisions.production_default: Relays are never paid by the protocol. Launch Operators are funded by written off-protocol commitments covering 12 months (MPE-OPS-051). Option (c) is an optional later feature behind the MPE-ECO-034 invariants. Option (d) is rejected.
decisions.reason: DUST is shielded and non-transferable and no code path credits fees to anyone (midnight-node/runtime/src/lib.rs:691,695 return (0, None); MPE-ECO-002). Relay quality is not checkable by a contract, and score attacks cut the cost of dominating a paid active set by over 99% (2026-cao-nymreputation, as cited in MPE-ECO-038 and MPE-OPS-034).
decisions.settled_by: o2's economic simulation showing at least 12 months of treasury runway with no grant draw; written Operator bids (s1 D4); procurement showing 8 organizations will sign (DEC-OPS-6).

decisions.title: Forward secrecy posture
options: (a) No forward-secrecy claim at launch; symmetric stream secrets
(b) Per-epoch hash progression of stream keys
(c) Encrypted-header Double Ratchet sessions with hybrid PQXDH setup

proposed_by.(a): g1, g2, g3, g4; DEC-PRV-4, DEC-CRY-1 recommended
proposed_by.(c): s2, s3; s1 and s4 conditional on a reviewed wrapper; MPE-CRY-028..035

decisions.prototype_default: (a): invitation-based symmetric profile (MPE-CRY-001), revocation rekey from fresh entropy (MPE-CRY-019), capability record stating no forward secrecy (MPE-CRY-026, MPE-PRV-026).
decisions.production_default: (a) for the broadcast bus; (c) as an optional pairwise profile, each claim gated by MPE-CRY-040 and MPE-VER-037. Option (b) is rejected.
decisions.reason: Static or stream-key encryption has no recipient-compromise forward secrecy (2022-barnes-rfc9180 section 9.1). Hash progression does not revoke a removed holder (MPE-CRY-019) and retained keys over a 48 h retention window defeat its secrecy claim (s2 R2). Ratchet secrecy holds only with erasure (2016-signal-double-ratchet-spec sections 8.1-8.4).
decisions.settled_by: DEC-CRY-1 check: run both profiles on identical workloads including broadcast fan-out, offline recovery, crash restore and retained-key compromise, and count KEY_GAP outcomes against the 48 h window.

decisions.title: Recognition mechanism
options: (a) Trial decryption of every Envelope, no Tag
(b) Per-publisher sequence PRF Tags with an expected-Tag lookahead window
(e) Encrypted-header trial under a capped key set
(f) Visible recognition Tag or FMD clue in the Visible Header

proposed_by.(a): g1, g3, g4, o3 R2; DEC-CRY-2, DEC-PUB-2(a), DEC-CON-2(b)
proposed_by.(b): o1, o3 R1, o4 (direct channels); DEC-CON-2(a) recommended

decisions.prototype_default: (d): 16 B salt and 16 B Tag in the clear prefix of the Sealed Body (new MPE-FMT-051), HMAC-SHA-256 under the recognition key, local test of every Envelope of the Shard, then authentication (MPE-CRY-013, MPE-CRY-014).
decisions.production_default: (d), kept only if it measurably beats (a) on recognition cost; otherwise (a).
decisions.reason: (b) loses a publisher after more than W skipped numbers (o3 R2 withdrew it; MPE-CON-008 exists only to report that loss). (c) groups an hour of traffic. (f) gives relays a per-Envelope string and is rejected by DEC-FMT-2. (d) is unlinkable without the key and costs one HMAC per key per Envelope: 256 x 10 = 2,560 evaluations per second.
decisions.settled_by: DEC-PUB-2 benchmark of (a) against (d) at 256 keys and 10 and 100 Envelopes/s on desktop and phone hardware; the MPE-PRV-004 key-privacy review of the exact construction.

decisions.title: Envelope lifetime and ordinary retention (48 h versus 7 days)
options: (b) 10-minute relay cache, 24 h optional store, 7 days if anchored
(d) 7-day complete replication (7 d default, 14 d maximum for o1)

proposed_by.(a): g1
proposed_by.(c): g3, s1, s3, s4; DEC-STO-1, DEC-FMT-5 recommended

decisions.prototype_default: (c): L_max = ordinary retention = 172,800 s on per-Shard Store Nodes; archives off.
decisions.production_default: (c), with an optional paid archive up to 7 days (MPE-STO-021) and the 14-day hard ceiling (MPE-FMT-033).
decisions.reason: Four proposals converge on 48 h, which covers a wallet offline overnight (o4 R2's objection to 1 h). At the byte cap one replica holds 65,536 x 172,800 = 11.3 GB per Shard; 7 days would hold 39.6 GB per Shard, tripled by the three Operators per Shard (P-STO-5). Offline periods longer than 48 h are reported as retention gaps (MPE-PUB-045), not hidden.
decisions.settled_by: Pilot measurement of Subscriber offline intervals and the share of resumes that hit a retention gap, compared against a threshold recorded in the course-change register (MPE-OPS-053); Store Node cost bids at 48 h and 7 d.

decisions.title: Operating rate (10 versus 50 per second)
options: (a) 10 Envelopes/s and 64 KiB/s per Shard, whichever binds first
(e) Ledger-lane rates of 1/s average, 10/s peak, or about 0.67/s

proposed_by.(a): g3; g2 worked load; s1, s2, s3, s4; DEC-PRF-1 and DEC-VER-2 recommended

decisions.prototype_default: (a), with (b) run as the P-PRF-28 comparison for 24 h and 100/s bursts for 60 s.
decisions.production_default: (a) per Shard; aggregate capacity grows only through the Shard count (DEC-011). The count ceiling rises to 50/s only on the settling evidence below.
decisions.reason: '10/s' and '50/s' are not comparable without sizes: g1's normalized 50/s mix is 41.39 KiB/s, inside the 64 KiB/s byte cap. The binding unknowns are per-Envelope verification and recognition CPU, which (a) caps.
decisions.settled_by: MPE-PRF-025 run with the selected admission verifier: adopt 50/s if edge CPU stays within P-PRF-14, propagation p99 within P-PRF-11 and timely delivery at or above 99.9%.

decisions.title: Relay admission: permissioned or permissionless
options: (a) Registry allow-list, removed only after a failed capture red team
(b) Contracted dedicated Operators plus open relaying
(c) Open relaying controlled by peer scoring

proposed_by.(a): g1, o4 (amended), o1 R2, s3 (roster); DEC-OPS-1(a), DEC-NET-7(a), DEC-SEC-1
proposed_by.(c): g2, g3, o1 R1, o2; DEC-OPS-1(c), DEC-NET-7(b)

decisions.prototype_default: Both modes implemented; (a) is the default against the mock Registry relay list (MPE-OPS-007); (c) runs only in red-team experiments.
decisions.production_default: (a) at launch with at least 8 organizations and at most 20% each (MPE-OPS-009, MPE-OPS-010); removal only after the MPE-OPS-008 red team at 1:1 Sybil identities fails to push canary delivery below 99.9% and the MPE-OPS-048 audit gate passes.
decisions.reason: Scoring is not a Sybil defence (2020-leastauthority-gossipsub-audit); configurations exist where a withholding peer keeps a positive score (2022-kumar-gossipsub-formal). Paid publication does not constrain relay identities (DEC-SEC-1).
decisions.settled_by: MPE-OPS-008 red team at 1, 3 and 5% targeted placement and at 1:1 identities under production scoring parameters.

decisions.title: Admission instrument (DUST ticket, RLN membership, NIGHT bond, blind stamps)
options: (a) DUST-paid Registry membership with a per-Envelope anonymous nullifier proof (RLN-style)
(c) Visible member key with signature and credit counter
(d) Issuer-signed permits or publicly verifiable blind-RSA stamps
(e) DUST fee per Event on the ledger

proposed_by.(a): o1, g3, s3, o2, o4; DEC-ECO-1(a) recommended
proposed_by.(d): s1, s2, s4; g2 R2 vote; DEC-ECO-1(d) fallback
proposed_by.(f): o2, o4, o3 Lane B; DEC-ECO-2(c)

decisions.prototype_default: (a) against the mock Ledger Adapter: simulated registration fee, revocation on equivocation, no bond; 512 B Admission Slot; pluggable verifier.
decisions.production_default: (a) with DUST registration paid from shielded DUST (MPE-ECO-007) and revocation (MPE-ECO-028); (f) disabled at launch; (d) with a 354 B object-bound stamp if (a) fails MPE-ECO-048.
decisions.reason: (b) is unlinkable only at one ticket per transaction, about 2 tickets/s at a 10% block share (o1 R2). (c) links every Envelope of a member (MPE-FMT-005). (d) gives the issuer a customer-to-Event map (o4 R2; leakage row L-U). (e) caps the whole chain at about 21 calls/s (MPE-ECO-003). (f): deployed Waku dropped its deposit (2024-revuelta-waku-latency) and contract-held NIGHT on mainnet is unknown.
decisions.settled_by: MPE-ECO-048 (proof fields at most 4,096 B, verification at most 10 ms on a 4-vCPU core); a demonstrated off-chain verifier for the selected proof (o1 spike); MPE-ECO-049 registration at most 16 KiB and 0.5 DUST.

decisions.title: Ledger-only operation, ledger fallback and bodies on the ledger
options: (a) Overlay from the first phase; ledger for membership and Anchors
(b) Ledger and Indexer lane first, overlay later
(d) Fallback by whole-feed gateways in overlay framing
(e) Fallback by Misc events read through contractEvents
(f) Fallback by a default-off Substrate notification protocol

proposed_by.(a): g1, g2, g3, o1, o2, o4, s1, s2, s3, s4; DEC-NET-1(a), DEC-OPS-7(b)
proposed_by.(d): s1, s2, s4, o1 R2; DEC-NET-2(a)

decisions.prototype_default: (a); gateway fallback as the Bus Node stream service (new MPE-NET-048); the ledger carrier (MPE-FMT-040..046) runs only against the mock adapter; no ledger-only mode.
decisions.production_default: (a); fallback order (d) then (e) as a labelled last resort on ledger 9, never automatic (MPE-PRV-013); (f) and (g) rejected. Sealed Bodies may appear in Misc logs only through (e); Registry contract state never holds a body (MPE-STO-001 rewritten).
decisions.reason: Public networks run ledger 8 (midnight-docs/docs/concepts/how-midnight-works/building-blocks.mdx:79-83), so (b) and (c) have no public network. The ledger lane shares 1,000,000 blockUsage bytes per 6 s slot (ledger-parameters-config.json:158; runtime/src/lib.rs:292) and carries 256 B Misc payloads (minokawa-compact/compiler/midnight-events.ss:71-74). MPE-STO-001 ('no ledger writes, including the Misc fallback') contradicted MPE-FMT-040..046 and MPE-CON-053; the BRIEF keeps bodies out of ledger state while naming a Misc fallback path.
decisions.settled_by: The ledger-9 mainnet date against the Phase 1 start; a written product need for latency under one slot or bodies over 205 B (g4 T1); Prototype delivery at least 99% with p99 at most 6 s at 200 nodes (g2).

decisions.title: Bus Node behaviour under a stale chain view
options: (a) Ignore every Envelope whose admission depends on chain state while the view is stale
(b) Keep forwarding Envelopes valid under cached eligible Registry state; never Reject on chain-dependent checks

proposed_by.(a): MPE-NET-018, MPE-FMT-031; g1 D1, o1 R2 D9
proposed_by.(b): MPE-SEC-035, MPE-OPS-021, MPE-NET-038, MPE-ECO-025; g1 D7, g3 D9, o4 R2 D8, s4 D9

decisions.prototype_default: (b): Accept Envelopes that validate against a cached root that is current or superseded less than P-ECO-5 ago and whose membership period ended less than P-ECO-5 ago (new MPE-ECO-051); Ignore Envelopes that need state the node lacks; never Reject on a chain- or clock-dependent check while stale.
decisions.production_default: Same as the Prototype.
decisions.reason: (a) turns any Ledger Adapter outage into a bus outage: MPE-NET-018's test (freeze the mock adapter, expect Ignore) and MPE-OPS-021's test (freeze the mock adapter, expect delivery) cannot both pass. (b) keeps o1 R2's rule that a lagging chain source must not graylist honest forwarders, and the stale-root bound limits forwarding under old state to 25 h.
decisions.settled_by: One frozen-adapter test asserting both continued delivery of cached-valid Envelopes and zero P4 changes; a stale-root test at P-ECO-4 + P-ECO-5.

decisions.title: GossipSub message id versus Envelope Identifier
options: (a) Message id = Envelope Identifier, which excludes the Admission Slot
(b) Message id = hash of every wire byte; Envelope Identifier kept for admission binding, deduplication and Anchors

proposed_by.(a): MPE-FMT-019, MPE-NET-010; s1, s3, s4, o2 R2; DEC-FMT-3(b)
proposed_by.(b): MPE-PUB-026; g1, o4, o1 R1; DEC-FMT-3(a); g1 R2 objection; MPE-CRY-005 'final wire identifier'

decisions.prototype_default: (b): message id = SHA-256 over a domain string and the complete wire bytes; Envelope Identifier (MPE-FMT-018) binds admission, keys application deduplication, inventories and Anchor leaves; the application seen-set records an Envelope Identifier only after Accept (new MPE-SEC-041).
decisions.production_default: Same as the Prototype.
decisions.reason: rust-libp2p inserts the message id into its duplicate cache before application validation (rust-libp2p/protocols/gossipsub/src/behaviour.rs:1983), sends IDONTWANT for it before validation (behaviour.rs:1950), and on Reject removes the message only from the message cache (behaviour.rs:991). Under (a) a peer that forwards an honest Sealed Body with a corrupted Admission Slot makes each receiver that sees the corrupted copy first drop the honest copy as a duplicate, and IDONTWANT extends the suppression one hop, for the price of one P4 penalty per receiver. Under (b) the corrupted copy has its own id. Alternative valid admissions of one body still resolve to one delivery through the seen-set (MPE-SEC-014).
decisions.settled_by: New MPE-SEC-042: inject corrupted-slot copies ahead of the honest copy; the honest Envelope reaches every eligible Subscriber within P-VER-6.

decisions.title: Shard count
options: (a) One feed with the shard field reserved

proposed_by.(a): g1, s1, s2, s3, s4; DEC-PUB-1(a), DEC-NET-4(a)

decisions.prototype_default: 1 operating Shard; the benchmark topology runs 8 (P-PRF-3).
decisions.production_default: 1 at launch; raised by the Registry (at most 8) after one Shard exceeds the PRF cap for 7 days and the per-Shard anonymity floor holds.
decisions.reason: Round 2 has nine votes for one feed (DEC-PUB-1). Each split divides the anonymity set and exposes per-Shard volume (o2 R2). Sharding does not reach mobile budgets: at 10 x 2 KiB per second one feed is 1.77 GB/day and one of eight Shards 221 MB/day, against 56-60 MB/day (g4, o3).
decisions.settled_by: MPE-PRF-021 measured Subscriber bytes at 1 and 8 Shards; PRV's anonymity floor (MPE-OPS-052 counts).

decisions.title: Mesh profile

proposed_by.(a): g1, g3, o1 R1, s2; rust-libp2p default (config.rs:83-86); DEC-PRF-2 recommended
proposed_by.(b): g2, o1 R2; DEC-NET-3 recommended; DEC-SEC-2

decisions.prototype_default: (b), heartbeat 1 s, gossip factor 0.25, prune backoff 60 s, flood publishing off; (a) as the mandatory MPE-PRF-010 comparison.
decisions.production_default: (b), unless the comparison shows (a) meets P-PRF-23 and P-PRF-24 at 200 nodes under a 20% cold-start Sybil attack; then (a).
decisions.reason: The Prototype gates include the 20% cold-start attack (MPE-PRF-032, MPE-VER-018) and an outbound quota of 4 (MPE-SEC-003); (b) is the profile evaluated under that attack (2020-vyzovitis-gossipsub). D_out = 4 forces an eclipse to own four dialled slots (2015-heilman-eclipse). The cost is planning egress of 5.24 against 3.93 Mbit/s at the byte cap, absorbed by the revised edge budget.
decisions.settled_by: MPE-PRF-010 comparison at 50, 200 and 1,000 nodes with identical sizes, churn and 20% Sybil cold start.

decisions.title: Size classes and Admission Slot width

proposed_by.(a): s1, s3, g2 R2, g3 R2
proposed_by.(d): g1, o1 R2, o4 R2; DEC-FMT-1 recommended

decisions.production_default: (d) if the measured A is at most 1,024 B; otherwise (d) without the 256 B class.
decisions.reason: One table serves both carriers (1, 4, 16, 64 Misc parts) and the 256 B class keeps full-feed cost low (o3 R2, g3 R2). If a Midnight-native proof runs to kilobytes (o2 R2 cites 2,912 B and 4,832 B transaction proofs), class 0 becomes mostly admission overhead, which is DEC-FMT-1's own reversal trigger.
decisions.settled_by: MPE-ECO-048 measured proof length; per-class anonymity-set simulation at the PRF load (DEC-FMT-1); payload-size histograms from pilot applications.

decisions.title: Outcome for conflicting use of one allowance (equivocation)
options: (a) Reject the second Envelope and record evidence
(b) Ignore the second Envelope, record evidence and emit AdmissionConflict

proposed_by.(a): MPE-ECO-020; o2, o1, o4
proposed_by.(b): MPE-SEC-018, MPE-SEC-019; s3, s4; DEC-SEC-4 recommended

decisions.prototype_default: (b); revocation through MPE-ECO-028.
decisions.production_default: (b); bond slashing only where DEC-007 (f) is enabled.
decisions.reason: The peer forwarding the second Envelope may be honest: in another partition it accepted that Envelope first. Reject would graylist honest peers when partitions heal. The equivocator is punished by revocation, not by mesh score.
decisions.settled_by: Partition simulation in MPE-SEC-018: spend one allowance on two bodies in two partitions, heal, and confirm no P4 change and an evidence record.

decisions.title: Unknown or foreign Envelope version
options: (a) Bind version to the topic; mismatch is Reject
(d) Accept N and N-1 in one mesh

proposed_by.(a): g1, o1 R2, s2, s3, g3, o2; DEC-FMT-4 recommended; MPE-FMT-023

decisions.prototype_default: (a); one version.
decisions.production_default: (a) with both versions' topics relayed for P-FMT-9 = 34 days (MPE-FMT-024); a governance deny-list entry yields Ignore (MPE-OPS-036).
decisions.reason: Topic names carry the major version (MPE-NET-006), so a v1 topic never legitimately carries v2 bytes; Ignore would let a neighbour inject junk without penalty. Running both topics gives o4's overlap without mixing versions in one mesh.
decisions.settled_by: MPE-FMT-024 upgrade simulation with no loss of unexpired old-version Envelopes.

decisions.title: Quota accounting inside one Admission Proof
options: (b) Byte weights: P-ECO-3(c) credit indices per Envelope
(c) Per-class limits committed in the membership leaf, one nullifier per Envelope

proposed_by.(a): o1, o4, s3; DEC-ECO-4(a)
proposed_by.(b): g3, g2, o2 R2; DEC-ECO-4(b) recommended; MPE-ECO-017
proposed_by.(c): Reconciliation of MPE-ECO-017 with MPE-FMT-003 and MPE-FMT-007

decisions.prototype_default: (c): limits (64, 16, 4, 1) per epoch for classes 0-3; size class bound into the nullifier domain.
decisions.production_default: (c); (b) only with a reviewed multi-nullifier circuit that fits P-ECO-11.
decisions.reason: (b) needs up to 64 distinct credit indices for a class-3 Envelope: 64 nullifier and share pairs (at least 4 KiB of public outputs) or 64 proofs, which a single fixed Admission Slot cannot carry; and P-ECO-2 = 10 is below the class-3 weight, so the lowest tier could never send class 3. (c) bounds bytes per member per epoch at 4 x 16 KiB, which exceeds DEC-ECO-4's 2x target by a factor of 2; that excess is accepted for the Prototype.
decisions.settled_by: DEC-ECO-4 class-mix simulation at the lowest tier; circuit size and verification time of a multi-nullifier variant against P-ECO-11 and P-ECO-12.

decisions.title: Durability of admission replay state
options: (a) Durably commit consumed allowances before forwarding
(b) In-memory caches with an accepted restart replay window
(c) Recover protection, or wait until affected authorizations expire, before live admission

proposed_by.(a): MPE-SEC-015; s3, s2 R2
proposed_by.(c): g3 alternative, s3 R1; MPE-STO-015, MPE-SEC-016; DEC-STO-7

decisions.prototype_default: (c) by waiting: in-memory nullifier and seen-set state; after every process start the Bus Node returns Ignore for live admission for P-ECO-7 = 140 s.
decisions.production_default: Same; (a) remains an optional configuration (MPE-SEC-015 rewritten as optional).
decisions.reason: Every allowance is permanently ineligible at most 140 s after acceptance (MPE-ECO-021), so waiting restores the invariant without a disk write on the forwarding path and without rollback detection, which SEC lists as unknown. A restarted node already waits 600 s before injecting local publications (MPE-NET-030).
decisions.settled_by: DEC-STO-7 check: crash and stale-backup restore at epoch boundaries; no consumed allowance accepted twice.

decisions.title: Tombstones
options: (a) Authenticated tombstones with a 48 h deadline

proposed_by.(a): o4; DEC-OPS-5(a)

decisions.prototype_default: Disabled; MPE-OPS-025 and MPE-OPS-026 move to PROD scope.
decisions.production_default: Optional, binding only Operators under the Operator Agreement; deletion within 24 h; every tombstone published; replay records untouched.
decisions.reason: With 48 h retention a 48 h deadline never deletes a body before ordinary expiry. A forged or captured deletion authority is a censorship mechanism, so the feature waits for OPS issuance rules.
decisions.settled_by: Counsel memos for Phase 1 jurisdictions (MPE-OPS-050); DEC-SEC-5 forgery and replay tests.

decisions.title: Governance authority over the Registry
options: (a) Bus steward set with time-locks and 7-day emergency expiry
(b) Midnight Root through Council and TC

proposed_by.(a): o4; s4 R2 reduced form; DEC-OPS-2(a)

decisions.prototype_default: Mock Registry with a single maintainer key; time-lock and expiry logic exercised in the Quint model only.
decisions.production_default: (a), handed to Council and TC or removed before the open-admission phase ends (MPE-OPS-020).
decisions.reason: Federated motions take 5 days (midnight-node/runtime/src/lib.rs:789), too slow to eject a relay injecting malformed objects (o4 R2). (d) has no ejection or emergency path. MPE-ECO-035 limits any maintainer to parameter changes.
decisions.settled_by: Quint invariants I1-I6 (o4); MPE-OPS-017 result on whether a maintenance authority can be time-locked on ledger 9.

decisions.title: First contact and fuzzy detection
options: (d) Dedicated intro inbox with a stricter rate tier

proposed_by.(a): s1, s2, s3, s4, g4; DEC-CRY-3, DEC-PUB-3, DEC-CON-8 recommended

decisions.prototype_default: (a); FMD disabled (MPE-CRY-037).
decisions.production_default: (a); (d) only as a separately reviewed profile.
decisions.reason: An open inbox is a harassment vector (o4 R2); FMD detection keys expose candidate subsets to the detector (2021-seres-fmdfalsepositives sections 1, 4-6; listed in catalog/PB3-receiver-privacy.jsonl, absent from papers.tsv).
decisions.settled_by: A written product requirement for unsolicited contact plus a red-team pass on the intro-tier rate limit.

decisions.title: Light and mobile reception
options: (c) Tag index or queries with decoys

proposed_by.(a): g1, g2, g4, s1, s2, s3, s4, o3 R2; DEC-PUB-5, DEC-CON-1, DEC-PRV-1

decisions.prototype_default: (a) only.
decisions.production_default: (a) by default; (b)-(e) only as labelled opt-in profiles (MPE-PUB-016) with their own claim register (MPE-PRV-037).
decisions.reason: No selective mode keeps selection privacy at a demonstrated cost (s4 R2); sender-chosen S-FMD rates do not enforce a floor (2022-penumbra-fmd-spec).
decisions.settled_by: MPE-PRF-021 Subscriber bytes per day against the 56-60 MB/day mobile budgets, then a measured OMR or PIR profile.

decisions.title: Contract consumption path and signature algorithm
options: (a) In-circuit publisher signature with a secret-derived nullifier, no Anchor
(b) Anchor inclusion through a historic-root check

proposed_by.(a): s3, s2, s1, o3 R2, o1 R2, o2 R2; DEC-CON-3(a)
proposed_by.(b): o1 R1, o3 R1, o2, o4, g3; DEC-CON-3(b)

decisions.prototype_default: (a) with (e), exercised against a mock contract with a nullifier set (MPE-VER-032).
decisions.production_default: (a) with (e) unless (f) proves cheaper in the measured circuit; (b) optional (MPE-CON-047).
decisions.reason: (a) needs no cross-contract call and puts authority in the circuit (s3 #1, o4 D3). The Compact standard library exposes plain Ed25519 verification (minokawa-compact/doc/api/CompactStandardLibrary/exports.md:993); its circuit cost against JubJub is unknown.
decisions.settled_by: Compile both authorization fixtures on a ledger-9 devnet; compare circuit size and proving time; zero unauthorized and duplicate effects in the MPE-VER-009 model.

decisions.title: Publish ingress and stem
options: (e) No anonymity claim from any stem

proposed_by.(a): g2, g3; DEC-NET-6

decisions.prototype_default: (a) with (e): one Bus Node chosen at random from two dialled (MPE-NET-033).
decisions.production_default: (a) kept only if the first-spy run shows lower precision than direct publication; no anonymity claim.
decisions.reason: The Dandelion++ bound assumes a random 4-regular anonymity graph unknown to the adversary (2018-fanti-dandelionpp sections 3.1, 4.1) and does not transfer to GossipSub meshes.
decisions.settled_by: MPE-VER-027 first-spy precision and recall for (a), (b) and direct publication at coalitions 1-20%.

decisions.title: Anchor granularity and history
options: (a) One Anchor per Shard per window
(b) One Anchor per window covering all Shards

proposed_by.(a): MPE-NET-041; o1, o2

decisions.prototype_default: (b) with (e): 60 s windows; payload of window number, root over per-Shard batch roots and per-Shard counts (new MPE-NET-050); 49 h, 2,940 records.
decisions.production_default: Same as the Prototype.
decisions.reason: (a) multiplies records by the Shard count and breaks the STO record bound at 8 Shards (8 x 10,080). Contracts reject expired Events (MPE-CON-046), so no live root older than L_max serves a consumer; clients verify older Anchors from Misc history, not live state.
decisions.settled_by: Ledger-9 measurement of reachable Anchor-state bytes (MPE-STO-030) and per-Anchor cost (MPE-VER-030).

decisions.title: Second-source reconciliation: MUST or SHOULD
options: (a) Reconciliation against an independent second source is mandatory in the Prototype
(b) Single source with sequence-gap detection; second source optional

proposed_by.(a): s1, o3 R2, o4 R2; MPE-SEC-021 and MPE-CON-037 (MUST); DEC-PUB-4, DEC-CON-5
proposed_by.(b): g1, g4, o1, o2; MPE-PUB-014 and MPE-PUB-015 (SHOULD), MPE-CON-036 (PROD SHOULD)

decisions.prototype_default: (a): MPE-PUB-014 and MPE-PUB-015 become POC MUST.
decisions.reason: Sequence gaps cannot reveal suppression of a whole publisher or of first contact (o3 R2 D9); the inventory costs 1.6% of feed bytes (DEC-PUB-4).
decisions.settled_by: Omission-injection simulation (MPE-PUB-014 verify) with measured overhead below 2% of feed bytes.

decisions.title: Delivery labels and attributes
options: (a) Exactly one label, gossip or final
(b) A stored label from retention receipts

proposed_by.(a): MPE-CON-015; o3

decisions.prototype_default: Three orthogonal attributes: finality (gossip or final, MPE-CON-015), carrier (overlay, gateway or ledger, new MPE-CON-057) and storage (stored when MPE-STO-012 holds).
decisions.production_default: Same as the Prototype.
decisions.reason: MPE-CON-015 requires exactly one of two labels, which a third 'stored' label or a fallback label would violate; the three properties vary independently.
decisions.settled_by: API inspection plus a test delivering one Event over each carrier, before and after anchoring, with and without three receipts.

decisions.title: Direction of node bandwidth budgets

proposed_by.(a): DEC-PRF-4 drafting assumption
proposed_by.(b): g3 R1 D5 planning model (egress); g2 egress budget

decisions.prototype_default: (b): 6 Mbit/s per direction per Shard for an Edge Bus Node, 24 Mbit/s per direction for a Full Bus Node.
decisions.reason: g3's 4 Mbit/s is its egress model (1.25 x 6 x 64 KiB/s); reading it as aggregate halves the budget. With D = 8 the same model gives 5.24 Mbit/s egress.
decisions.settled_by: Two-direction packet capture at the byte cap under both mesh profiles (MPE-PRF-005).

decisions.title: Phase numbering and the Prototype boundary
options: (a) VER: Phase 0 evidence and models, 1 local Prototype and simulations, 2 integration and pilot, 3 production
(b) OPS: Phase 0 models, simulation and Prototype, 1 permissioned pilot, 2 permissioned production, 3 open admission, 4 handover

proposed_by.(a): DEC-VER-1; s4, g1, g2

fixes.text:
### MPE-FMT-001a Fixed-width visible layout
The MPE client library shall encode every Envelope field outside the Sealed Body as a fixed-width field at a fixed per-version offset.
- Pattern: ubiquitous
- Scope: POC
- Priority: MUST
- Source: D1; g1, s2, s3, s4, o1-R2, o4-R2; `2012-bitmessage-protocol-specification` (varint object header)
- Rationale: Each Envelope has exactly one legal byte string, so parsing is unambiguous.
- Verify: test, decode and re-encode every MPE-FMT-049 vector and compare the bytes for equality.
- Status: settled

### MPE-FMT-001b No variable encodings outside the Sealed Body
The MPE client library shall emit no optional field, extension field, length prefix, variable-length integer or self-describing encoding outside the Sealed Body.
- Pattern: ubiquitous
- Scope: POC
- Priority: MUST
- Source: D1; g1, s3, s4; `2020-vac-waku2-message-spec` (protobuf is not canonical)
- Rationale: A new field requires a new version and topic (register DEC-015).
- Verify: inspection, review the wire specification; test, every fuzzed Envelope that carries such a construct fails MPE-FMT-006 or MPE-FMT-007.
- Status: settled

### MPE-CRY-008 Random stream secrets
When a private stream is created, the MPE client library shall obtain its P-CRY-1-byte stream secret from the operating-system cryptographic random-number interface.
- Pattern: event
- Scope: POC
- Priority: MUST
- Source: D3; g4 R1 D3; s2 R1 D3; o3 R1 D3; `2021-len-partitioningoracle`, section 1
- Rationale: Human-chosen passphrases face a guessing threat that random capabilities do not.
- Verify: inspection, stream creation requests exactly P-CRY-1 bytes from the configured interface (getrandom on Linux); test, an injected interface failure produces the MPE-CRY-009 result.
- Status: settled

### MPE-PUB-006 Random private audience keys
The MPE client library shall obtain every private audience key as 32 bytes from the operating-system cryptographic random-number interface.
- Pattern: ubiquitous
- Scope: POC
- Priority: MUST
- Source: D3; g4 D3; `2021-len-partitioningoracle` (ChaCha20-Poly1305 is not key-committing); see canonical MPE-CRY-008
- Rationale: Low-entropy keys allow guessing topics and multi-key openings.
- Verify: inspection, the API offers no passphrase input for private topics and key generation calls the operating-system interface.
- Status: settled

### MPE-OPS-033a Aggregated counter release
Where Bus Node counters are published, the Bus Node shall release them only as aggregates computed across at least P-OPS-16 share keepers, none of which receives an individual Bus Node's counter value.
- Pattern: optional
- Scope: PROD
- Priority: SHOULD
- Source: D7; o4 D7; `2016-jansen-safely-measuring-tor`
- Rationale: Load can be measured without exposing any single relay's activity.
- Verify: inspection, review the counter-export path; test, capture share-keeper inputs and confirm each is a blinded share.
- Status: open (DEC-OPS-4)

### MPE-OPS-033b Differential-privacy budget for counters
Where Bus Node counters are published, the Bus Node shall add noise that gives each published counter a differential-privacy epsilon of at most P-OPS-18.
- Pattern: optional
- Scope: PROD
- Priority: SHOULD
- Source: D7; o4 D7; `2018-mani-tor-usage-privacy-preserving` txt L505
- Rationale: Aggregation alone does not bound what a published count reveals about one user.
- Verify: analysis, compute epsilon from the configured noise distribution and sensitivity; test, the noise sampler matches that distribution (KS test, p > 0.01).
- Status: open (DEC-OPS-4)

### MPE-OPS-043 Evidence freeze
When the Phase 0 exit review starts, MPE shall record the target network's ledger version, runtime `spec_version` and the pinned revision of every Midnight component the bus depends on.
- Pattern: event
- Scope: PROD
- Priority: MUST
- Source: D10; s4 D10; o4 R2; o3 R2; `midnight-node/Cargo.lock:7894`
- Rationale: The tag, the lockfile and the documentation disagree, for example on the 1 KiB log limit.
- Verify: inspection, compare the claim register against a live RPC `spec_version` query.
- Status: settled

### MPE-OPS-046 Measured Registry costs

- Priority: MUST

- Scope: POC
- Priority: SHOULD

While an unexpired Envelope is retained by at least one configured source that answers the Subscriber's requests, MPE shall deliver that Envelope to the Subscriber's client library at least once.

- Status: settled

While the relay allow-list is inactive, MPE shall eject a relay only on published evidence that P-OPS-16 independent monitors measured its canary delivery below P-OPS-5 for P-OPS-12, or on a malformed Anchor it signed.

- Priority: MUST

- Priority: SHOULD
- Source: D7; o4 D7

- Priority: SHOULD

### MPE-SEC-022 Authenticate Registry read results
If an Indexer result is not confirmed by Registry state read from P-NET-14 independent chain sources at a finalized block, then the Indexer adapter shall exclude it from admission and Anchor authorization.

The Bus Node shall set the GossipSub message id to SHA-256 over a fixed MPE domain string and the complete received Envelope bytes.

- Scope: POC
- Priority: MUST

### MPE-NET-017 Ignore outcome

The Bus Node shall return Reject for an Envelope of size class c unless its Admission Proof shows a credit index below the class-c per-epoch limit committed in the membership leaf.

The MPE client library shall derive each Admission Proof nullifier from the admission secret, epoch number, size class and credit index under one domain-separated hash.

- Scope: POC
- Priority: MUST

### MPE-ECO-020 Equivocation recorded without penalty
If an Envelope carries a nullifier already accepted with a different Envelope Identifier, then the Bus Node shall return Ignore and record both Envelopes as equivocation evidence.

- Priority: MUST

- Priority: MUST

- Priority: MUST
- Source: D6; g3 R1 D6; s3 R1 D6; MPE-FMT-029

The MPE client library shall mark a delivered Event `stored` only after validating compatible retention receipts from at least P-STO-5 distinct Operators.

- Priority: MUST

- Scope: PROD
- Priority: MUST
- Source: D5; g3 R1 D5; register DEC-027

Where durable replay state is configured, the Bus Node shall commit each consumed publication allowance to durable storage before forwarding its Envelope.

- Priority: MUST

The MPE client library shall authenticate the Network Identifier, Visible Header bytes 0 to 7, and the Sealed Body's salt, nonce and Tag as AEAD associated data.
